learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Knowledge about the application of matrix calculations to solve problems of n degrees of freedom.
Capacity for the calculation of forces and deformations in structures with articulated and rigid nodes.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Mastery of the concept of equilibrium applied to each part of the structure.
Mastery of the concept of stiffness.

syllabus_topics: Calculation of forces in isostatic articulated-node structures
Calculation of displacements in isostatic articulated-node structures
Calculation of forces and displacements in hyperstatic articulated-node structures
Principle of virtual work in rigid nodes
Introduction of applied loads inside members

assessment_methods.method: Group work test on cooperative actions (articulated)
Group work test on cooperative actions (rigid nodes)
Group work test on cooperative actions (matrix)

assessment_rules: All tests are graded out of 10. Attendance and completion of laboratory practices are mandatory to pass the course; their grade is retained for subsequent years and can be repeated to improve it. For progressive evaluation, the overall grade is calculated as 10% from lab practices, 10% from the geometric mean of cooperative actions tests, 20% from the Topic 2 control, 20% from the Topic 3 control, and 40% from the Final Exam. A minimum grade of 3 is required on the Final Exam in progressive evaluation; if not met, the final grade cannot exceed 4.9. For global or extraordinary evaluation, the overall grade is the greater of the progressive evaluation grade and a final evaluation consisting of 90% Final Exam and 10% laboratory practices. Laboratory practice tests are non-recoverable if sessions are not attended.
